md_changes.file_patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+---
+emoji: 🏷️
+name: Issue Triage
+description: Triage newly opened or edited issues with labels, assignment, and a short note
+on:
+  issues:
+    types: [opened, edited]
+engine: copilot
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+safe-outputs:
+  add-labels:
+    allowed:
+      - OS-Linux
+      - OS-MacOS
+      - OS-Windows
+      - Container-Process
+      - Container-MicroVM
+      - Container-VM
+      - Container-WSLC
+      - Container-Session
+      - Container-Hyperlight
+      - Area-SDK-Configuration
+      - Area-SDK-Policy
+      - Area-Executor-Schema
+      - Area-SDK-Api
+      - Area-Executor-LXC
+      - Area-Executor-WXC
+      - Area-Build-Rust
+      - Area-Build-TypeScript
+      - Area-Test-SDK
+      - Area-Test-Executor
+    max: 6
+  remove-labels:
+    allowed: [Needs-Triage]
+  assign-to-user:
+    allowed:
+      - jsidewhite
+      - mgudgin
+      - SohamDas2021
+      - bbonaby
+      - huzaifa-d
+      - adpa-ms
+      - richiemsft
+    max: 2
+  add-comment:
+    max: 1
+---
+
+# Issue Triage
+
+## Task
+
+Read the triggering issue title and body and triage by meaning, not keyword matching.
+
+### Labels to apply
+
+- Apply only labels from the configured `add-labels.allowed` list.
+- Apply the OS-*, Container-*, and Area-* labels the issue is genuinely about.
+- Ignore terms mentioned only in passing (for example in file paths, build flags, or examples).
+- Understand synonyms and short forms. Treat "Mac", "Mac x64", "Mac ARM", "Mac aarch64", "macOS", "darwin", and "Seatbelt" as the macOS backend.
+- Do not invent labels.
+
+### Owner assignment map
+
+Assign matching owner(s) with `assign_to_user` using this map:
+
+| Owner (login) | Area |
+|---|---|
+| @jsidewhite | AppContainer / BaseContainer / process isolation/container |
+| @mgudgin | AppContainer / BaseContainer / process isolation/container |
+| @bbonaby | AppContainer / BaseContainer / process isolation/container / networking / firewall / DNS / proxy / iptables |
+| @SohamDas2021 | Linux / LXC / WSLC / Bubblewrap (bwrap) / proxy on Linux / iptables |
+| @huzaifa-d | MicroVM / NanVix / Hyperlight / Windows Sandbox |
+| @adpa-ms | IsolationSession / session isolation |
+| @richiemsft | macOS / Seatbelt |
+
+Rules:
+
+- Assign more than one owner only if the issue genuinely spans multiple areas.
+- If nothing fits, assign no one.
+
+### Needs-Triage handling
+
+- If at least one OS/Container/Area label was applied OR at least one owner was assigned, remove `Needs-Triage` with `remove_labels`.
+- If nothing clearly matched, keep `Needs-Triage`.
+
+### Comment requirement
+
+Post one short triage comment with `add_comment` that:
+
+- states which labels were applied (if any),
+- states which owner(s) were assigned (if any),
+- explicitly says when nothing clearly matched and `Needs-Triage` was left in place.
+
+Use `noop` only if the issue cannot be analyzed from the available title/body content.

commits.message:
Fix issue-triage auth: use copilot-requests permission instead of PAT (#617)

The gh-aw issue-triage workflow failed to triage new issues (e.g. #612,
run 28873492335) at the activation step with "None of the following
secrets are set: COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN" - the Copilot engine had no
inference credential configured.

Add copilot-requests: write to the workflow permissions so the engine
authenticates with the built-in Actions token (github.token), per the
gh-aw auth docs. No PAT or org secret required; requests are org-billed.

Regenerating the lock from source also picks up two fixes that were
stranded in the previously hand-edited (stale) lock:
- mgudgin is now in the live assign_to_user list (was only in the .md)
- the leftover eyes-reaction step (no longer in the .md) is dropped

Co-authored-by: Huzaifa Danish <modanish@microsoft.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
Triage: reduce failure-report noise, scope repos, and guard against false missing_data (#619)

* Triage: allow external-contributor issues, stop failure-report noise

Set tools.github.min-integrity to 'unapproved' so the triage agent can
read issues from external contributors (CONTRIBUTOR / FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR),
which were previously filtered out by the public-repo default of 'approved'.
This is gh-aw's recommended level for community triage; the workflow's
locked safe-outputs (fixed label list, fixed assignee table, hard caps)
keep the blast radius to a mislabel even on untrusted input.

Also set safe-outputs.report-failure-as-issue to false so blocked or
missing-data runs no longer auto-file tracking issues.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Triage: scope integrity guard + safe-output sink to this repo

Add tools.github.allowed-repos set to the github.repository expression so
the GitHub integrity guard policy (and the safe-output write sink) are
scoped to microsoft/mxc instead of the default "all". Least-privilege
hardening from adversarial review: bounds the blast radius if the MCP
token is ever broader-scoped. The compiler only accepts "all", "public",
or the github.repository expression here, so the expression form is used.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Guard triage agent against false missing_data

Add an explicit prompt instruction so the agent never emits missing_data (or claims content is filtered/unreadable) after a successful issue read. Root cause of the #611 triage miss was an intermittent agent hallucination, not integrity filtering: trial reproductions against #611 under the same config triaged correctly 2/2.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

 Use `noop` only if the issue cannot be analyzed from the available title/body content.
+
+### Do not falsely report missing or filtered content
+
+- The triggering issue number is provided in the context above. Always read the issue title and body with the GitHub tools first.
+- If that read returns a title or body, you HAVE the content: proceed to triage it. Do not stop.
+- Never emit `missing_data`, and never claim the content is "filtered", "unreadable", "blocked", or "missing", when the issue read returned content.
+- `missing_data` is reserved for a genuine tool or API failure where no title or body could be retrieved at all. If a read fails, retry once before concluding anything is missing.

commits.message:
Fix gh-aw triage: gateway crash hotfix + fill owner-map assignment gap (#639)

* Fix gh-aw triage gateway crash: emit allowed-repos as an array

The guard policy rendered allowed-repos as a bare string
(repos: microsoft/mxc), which MCP Gateway rejects at startup:
allow-only.repos string must be all or public. A specific repo must be
an array. Using YAML list form makes the lock emit repos as a JSON
array, which the gateway accepts.

This was a production outage: every triage run since the bare-string
form merged failed at the agent job because the gateway would not start.
gh aw compile is static and did not catch it; verified the fix with
gh aw trial (gateway started clean, agent read the issue and produced
valid safe-outputs).

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Add SDK/schema/build/test area owners and theelliotm to triage owner map

Fills the assignment gap where SDK/schema/build/test area labels had no
owner in the agentic triage prompt. Adds theelliotm to the
assign-to-user allow-list and four rows to the owner map:

- mgudgin:    SDK configuration / policy
- huzaifa-d:  SDK API / executor schema / TypeScript build
- bbonaby:    Rust build
- theelliotm: SDK / executor test infrastructure

Verified with gh aw trial against #613: agent assigned bbonaby +
huzaifa-d (cap 2) and removed Needs-Triage.

commits.message:
Enable community issue triage: open roles + integrity gates (#646)

Allow the gh-aw issue-triage workflow to run for external community
issues (author permission=read, author_association=NONE):

- roles: add `read` so read-permission authors pass the activation gate
  (previously only admin/maintainer/write activated; external filers skipped)
- min-integrity: none so the agent can read content from NONE-association
  authors (unapproved only reaches CONTRIBUTOR/FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR)

Trial-verified against microsoft/mxc#553 (read, NONE author):
activation + agent both succeeded and produced a real triage decision
(labels + assignee + comment). Risk is bounded to reversible
mislabel/misassign: safe-outputs only (no code/secret access),
repo-scoped MCP gateway guard, report-failure-as-issue: false.

Co-authored-by: Huzaifa Danish <modanish@microsoft.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
